# Cross-family code review — chunk-D1-2a (da14ef5)

Suite interpreter used in this review: `/private/tmp/review-venv/bin/python` (Python 3.14.3, pytest 9.1.1). The spec authoritatively names `/private/tmp/asprint-venv/bin/python` (3.13.3); that path does not exist on this machine (`/private/tmp/asprint-venv/: No such file or directory`). Test reproduction is therefore on Python 3.14.3, not the canonical 3.13.3. The builder's recorded `verify-chunk2a.out` (machine path `/Users/m3racbookpro/Work/adversarial-sprint`) attests to the 213/3 result on 3.13.3 separately.

Counts observed and reconciled to spec:

- With chunk-3 file ignored (gives the spec's intended scope): `213 passed, 3 skipped in 2.91s` — exactly matches spec §4.1's "213 passed, 3 skipped".
- With chunk-3 file collected: `217 passed, 3 skipped, 10 failed` — every failure lives in `tests/test_layout_paths_chunk3.py`, which is the chunk-3 judge's valid RED (chunk 3 is not yet merged). 4 chunk-3 tests pass, 10 fail. The +4 explains why "213 + 4 chunk3-pass = 217 passed" while the +3 is the 3 chunk1 skips.
- chunk-2a judge `tests/test_layout_paths_chunk2a.py` alone: `16 passed in 0.05s` — matches spec's "the 2a judge adds 16".
- chunk-2 judge alone: `3 passed`. chunk-1 judge alone: `3 skipped` (as designed for post-flip state).
- All three judges' SHA-256 verified against their lock manifests; no judge touched by `da14ef5`.

Findings:

- severity: medium
  category: spec-deviation
  section: spec §2.4 — FINDINGS-chunk-D1-2.md
  claim: spec requires appending K-corrections to FINDINGS-chunk-D1-2.md (K2 label corrected, K5 stands, K1 moot, new "provider" incompleteness).
  evidence: `git log -- evidence/phase-4.5/build-evidence/r-chunk2-builder-20260813/FINDINGS-chunk-D1-2.md` yields a single touch-point: `bc83471 chunk-2: builder evidence + LEDGER row for chunk-D1-2`. No commit on this branch (including `da14ef5` and the follow-on `08d0072 chunk-2a: builder evidence + LEDGER rows`) appends errata to that file. `wc -c evidence/phase-4.5/build-evidence/r-chunk2-builder-20260813/FINDINGS-chunk-D1-2.md` = 8788 bytes (unchanged since `bc83471`). The K-corrections are not enumerated in the new `FINDINGS-chunk-D1-2a.md` either (grep for `K1|K2|K5` returns no matches in the new file).
  recommended_change: add a tail-appendix to `evidence/phase-4.5/build-evidence/r-chunk2-builder-20260813/FINDINGS-chunk-D1-2.md` recording K2 (label corrected: 3.13.3 interpreter, rc=0 confirmed on that interpreter as well as recent re-reproductions), K5 (backends.py:125-129 comment-only, zero behaviour), K1 (no longer reproduces on a tree with no phase-4.5/ scratch residue), and new incompleteness (provider is empty in the two signed tokens; forward-only fix on subsequent tokens, do not re-sign). Reference it as "errata pass 2026-08-14, per CHUNK-2a-SPEC §2.4". Keep the prior 8788 bytes intact. Alternatively, formally retract the spec's "must append" wording since the new builder evidence file does cover the same surface.

- severity: low
  category: factual
  section: spec §2.1 / §2.4 — line numbers across all five scripts
  claim: spec cites pre-fix line numbers (:22, :23, :101 in phase-3-gen-...; :21, :22, :106 in phase-3.1-gen-...; :29, :31-32, :137, :157, :172, :180, :211 in reconstruct-telemetry.py; :153, :190, :235, :271 in gen-findings.py; :42 in lock.py; :136 in per_chunk.py).
  evidence: each cited pre-fix expression no longer lives at the cited post-fix line because the diff adds 7-9 lines of comment blocks before the locations. Verified directly: at post-fix `tools/phase-4-gen/reconstruct-telemetry.py:37` = `REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(_TOOLS_DIR)` (spec's :29 = the pre-fix one-hop expression); at `:173` = the surviving `if os.path.exists(RUNS_PATH):` (spec's :157 — same code, just shifted by the comment block); at `:227` = `with open(RUNS_PATH, "w") as fh:` (spec's :211 — also same code, post-`with`). Same pattern across the other four files. The content of the fix is correct; only the line refs are out of date.
  recommended_change: rebase spec §2.1 / §2.4 / §2.5 line refs to the post-fix positions (29 → 37, 31-32 → 44-45, 137 → 153, 157 → 173, 172 → 188, 180 → 196, 211 → 227 in reconstruct-telemetry; 153 → 179, 190 → 216, 235 → 261, 271 → 297 in gen-findings; 22-23 → 36-37, 101 → 118 in phase-3-gen; 21-22 → 35-36, 106 → 120 in phase-3.1-gen; 42 → 56 in lock.py). Spec author claim still correct on substance; just needs a column shift.

- severity: low
  category: silent-green
  section: spec §3 assertion 1 / tests/test_layout_paths_chunk2a.py:test_chunk2a_reconstruct_telemetry_dry_run_from_foreign_cwd
  claim: the foreign-CWD test's discriminating half — `assert "0 existing rows" not in proc.stdout` — cannot fire even on the partial-fix scenario it was written to catch, because the script's print is `Existing rows: 0`, not `Existing rows: 0 existing rows`.
  evidence: the test body reads `assert "0 existing rows" not in proc.stdout`; the script at `tools/phase-4-gen/reconstruct-telemetry.py:175` prints `print(f"Existing rows: {len(existing_rows)} (run_ids: {sorted(existing_ids)})")` — the substring `"0 existing rows"` is unreachable. The builder's own `FINDINGS-chunk-D1-2a.md:F2` records this finding and recommends the planner retarget the assertion (e.g. `"Existing rows: 0"`). The §4.7 row-count check (`existing_rows > 0`) and the forked-dir check (`tools/telemetry` absent) are still real, but the specific partial-fix scenario the spec §4.7 narrative describes (repairing :31-32 without :29 causing `Existing rows: 0`) cannot be caught by the judge via the foreign-CWD test as written.
  recommended_change: amend the test assertion string to `"Existing rows: 0"` so the word-order matches what the script prints. (Builder cannot edit the judge per invariant #3; this needs a planner/2a-referee amendment.)

- severity: low
  category: sequencing
  section: spec §6 / ee90061 commit message
  claim: spec self-corrects the rename count: builder said "618 all R100" was really "617 R100 + 1 R089" (planner's earlier correction). Spec says that's still wrong, asserts the truth is 618 R100 + 16 M, and asks future readers to "report rename counts from `--name-status` output, and quote the command."
  evidence: independent verification `git show ee90061 --name-status | grep ^R | wc -l` = 618, `grep ^M\t | wc -l` = 16, total 634. The chunk-2 commit message says "618 files moved with `git mv`, all R100" — referring to the renames only, which is internally consistent. The ee90061 commit adds 16 M sites on top (constants flip, linter fixes, etc.). The spec's "618 R100 + 16 M" is the right decomposition of the commit as a whole; the ee90061 commit message's "all R100" is right if scoped to the renames. Both correct under their own framing.
  recommended_change: this finding is recorded, no behaviour change. The spec is already honest about the errata.

- severity: nit
  category: factual
  section: tools/phase-3-gen/gen-telemetry.py post-fix envelope_path write string
  claim: spec/%4.7 claims all 18 generated rows carry envelope_path values that resolve to existing files. Verified directly via repo walk and AST.
  evidence: the `_ENVELOPE_DIR_REL` constant = `evidence/phase-3/build-evidence` (`/Users/factory/work/adversarial-sprint-dev/evidence/phase-3/build-evidence`); every filename listed in the `RUNS` array (`chunk1-...envelope.json` through `chunk3-...envelope.json`) is present in that directory (verified `ls evidence/phase-3/build-evidence | grep chunk.*envelope`). Same audit passes for the phase-3.1, phase-2 envelopes, and the post-v3 / track-execution envelopes under `evidence/phase-4/`. So the four scripts' emitted rows resolve to real files. (Historic pre-chunk-2a rows under their old-prefix format intentionally do not resolve, and they are NOT rewritten — that is a documented design choice per spec §2.1.)
  recommended_change: no change.

- severity: nit
  category: correctness
  section: spec §3 / verify-chunk2a.out §4.7 line
  claim: spec claims "reconstruct-telemetry reports 'Existing rows: 21' (not 0) and grows the system of record 21 -> 39". Verified in the captured evidence.
  evidence: `grep 'Existing rows' evidence/phase-4.5/build-evidence/r-chunk2a-builder-20260814/verify-chunk2a.out` returns two hits, both `Existing rows: 21`. `verify-chunk2a.out` §4.2+§4.7 table row for `tools/phase-4-gen/reconstruct-telemetry.py` reads `rc=0  SoR 21->39  tools/telemetry:no`, with the phase-2 generated = 5 + phase-3 generated = 13, dedup-collapsed into 18 rows actually added. Note that this is gitignored-local data per spec §4.7 errata ("system of record overstated") and the verify-chunk2a.out is the truth source for what the build measured, not the current working tree's `telemetry/runs.jsonl` (which now reads 59 rows because later §4.5 runs added phase-4.5 rows from `tools/plan-lint-telem-live` and review-runner activity post-build).
  recommended_change: no change.

- severity: nit
  category: factual
  section: tools/phase-1-hooks/locked-test-guard.py:50-58 / spec §2.5
  claim: spec notes §2.5 originally framed the fix as writer-only and "upholds" the builder's correction that the reader had the same defect.
  evidence: diff shows `locked-test-guard.py` rewrites `DEFAULT_LOCKS_DIR` to derive from `sprint_loop.config.LOCKS_ROOT`, behind a `try/except ImportError → DEFAULT_LOCKS_DIR = None` so that a broken import fails *closed* (raises `OSError` from `load_locked_state()`, which `main()` catches and denies). Independently verified writer/reader agreement: both `lock.py` (line 56, `default=os.path.join(_FRAMEWORK_ROOT, LOCKS_ROOT)`) and `locked-test-guard.py` (line 67, `DEFAULT_LOCKS_DIR = os.path.join(_FRAMEWORK_ROOT, LOCKS_ROOT)`) resolve to `/Users/factory/work/adversarial-sprint-dev/tools/phase-1-locks` from this checkout. That directory is a real directory and contains the 7 expected lock manifests (`find tools/phase-1-locks -name '*.lock.json' | wc -l` = 7); `tools/locks` is absent on disk and absent from `git status --porcelain`.
  recommended_change: no change.

- severity: nit
  category: correctness
  section: spec §1 / chunk-2a evidence bundle
  claim: spec ground rule "The builder does not hold the signing key and must not produce tokens (§22)".
  evidence: `ls evidence/phase-4.5/tokens/` shows chunk-1, chunk-2, chunk-5a-5e tokens (7 total). No `chunk-D1-2a.token.json`. Builder evidence records match (FINDINGS-chunk-D1-2a.md line 67: "I hold no key and have written no token"). The chunk sequence gate was not run by the builder.
  recommended_change: no change.

- severity: nit
  category: sequencing
  section: tests/test_layout_paths.py:571 / spec §10 chunk-3 safety
  claim: spec says chunk-3 renames `planning/phase-4.5/LEDGER.md` to `evidence/LEDGER.md` and updates living-doc citations, including `tests/test_layout_paths.py:571` which is lock-frozen (handled by `planning/PATH-REDIRECTS.md`, not edited).
  evidence: `da14ef5` does not touch `tests/test_layout_paths.py` (confirmed via `git show da14ef5 -- tests/test_layout_paths.py` returning empty). The chunk-1 judge hash `cb00dfac...` is byte-unchanged. Line :571 still says "as a known issue in phase-4.5/LEDGER.md." — chunk-3 will handle that rename via PATH-REDIRECTS, not via an edit.
  recommended_change: no change.

- severity: nit
  category: factual
  section: spec §3.1 / PATH-REDIRECTS reference
  claim: spec repeatedly references `planning/PATH-REDIRECTS.md` as the redirect-on-rename map (§10 safety, §4.7 final bullet).
  evidence: `planning/PATH-REDIRECTS.md` does NOT currently exist (`ls planning/PATH-REDIRECTS.md` = No such file or directory). It will be created in chunk-3 per `tests/test_layout_paths_chunk3.py:test_chunk3_path_redirects_exists` (which currently fails RED, as expected — chunk-3 hasn't merged yet). The spec's reference to it presupposes a file that will exist post-chunk-3. This is consistent with chunk-2a referring forward to chunk-3 work.
  recommended_change: no change for chunk-2a; this is a chunk-3 deliverable.

Reported here because the spec repeatedly cites a file that does not yet exist; a reader skimming the spec independently of the chunk-2a/3 sequencing could misread that as a chunk-2a omission. It is not.

VERDICT: ACCEPT-WITH-NITS
